title: Audio request scalar admission diagnostics: bounded original writer findings

claims.Finding: The captured initializer constructs the fixed 80-entry request pool/free-index arrangement and writes FreeCount at 0x140AD9390 to 80 at 0x14000DBA1. This establishes the diagnostic pool capacity for this executable.
claims.Limitations: This static initializer is distinct from the later runtime reset. It is not evidence that every runtime reset restores the free count or that unobserved aliases cannot modify it.

claims.Finding: This eight-byte setter writes 1 to the admission inhibit byte at 0x140AD93C0 and returns. The diagnostic mask reports this observed byte as bit 1.
claims.Limitations: No caller timing or playback outcome is inferred from the setter alone.

claims.Finding: This eight-byte setter writes 0 to the admission inhibit byte at 0x140AD93C0 and returns.
claims.Limitations: A cleared inhibit byte leaves the two scalar limit checks and downstream resource requirements independent.

claims.Finding: The request allocator rejects nonzero inhibit, signed FreeCount <=16, or signed IntervalCount >24. On admission it decrements FreeCount, increments IntervalCount and computes the selected request address from a free-index stack with 56-byte record stride. These comparisons define diagnostic mask bits 1, 2 and 4.
claims.Limitations: These are observed reservation gates. A clear mask does not prove a resource exists, a later reservation succeeds, or playback occurs; the trainer never calls this allocator.

claims.Finding: This IOP request path repeats the inhibit, signed FreeCount <=16 and signed IntervalCount >24 admission checks, then performs the same counter decrement/increment before populating its admitted request. This is a second direct writer supporting the shared admission-counter interpretation.
claims.Limitations: The bounded claim covers the captured scalar admission path. Request state transitions and backend playback outcomes are not exposed by the new diagnostic.

claims.Finding: The captured runtime reset writes IntervalCount at 0x140AD93C4 to zero, clears the admission inhibit byte at 0x140AD93C0 and resets four request-list root globals. Its captured body contains no FreeCount write.
claims.Limitations: This is a direct-body observation rather than an exclusion of writes through all callees. The diagnostic does not traverse these roots or infer lifetime safety from this reset.

limits: Six newly captured function bodies only; prior Voice bodies 0x1401DE230 and 0x1401DD8D0 retain their original study attribution.
Selected direct writers are not a whole-program alias, thread, concurrency or lifetime proof.
The production feature samples only three fixed scalars and exact writer code; no native instructions or audio objects are executed or traversed.
